credits: Episode 6 (mid-credits): A third, hidden personality, Jake Lockley, kidnaps Harrow from a mental hospital and shoots him on Khonshu's orders.

entries.title: Ms. Marvel
entries.label: Story
meta: Aired: June 8 to July 13, 2022 · 6 episodes · Phase 4 · Set in: 2026 · Watch after: Moon Knight (essential before The Marvels)
entries.story: Kamala Khan, a Pakistani American teenager in Jersey City and Captain Marvel's biggest fan, puts on a bangle inherited from her great-grandmother and gains the power to create glowing hard-light shapes. The bangle draws the attention of the Clandestines, beings from another dimension (the Noor dimension) who want to use it to go home, even if it destroys Earth. Kamala's journey takes her to Karachi, Pakistan, and back in time to the 1947 Partition of India, where she discovers her family's history and her own role in it. Back in Jersey City, she protects her friend Kamran from the Department of Damage Control, earning her family's acceptance as the hero "Ms. Marvel." Her friend Bruno discovers there is "something different" in her genes, "like a mutation," while the theme from the 1990s X-Men cartoon plays: the first hint that mutants exist in the main universe.
credits: Episode 1 (mid-credits): Damage Control agents find footage of Kamala's powers.
Episode 6 (mid-credits): Kamala's bangle glows and she swaps places with Captain Marvel, who appears in her bedroom. (This leads directly into The Marvels.)

entries.title: She-Hulk: Attorney at Law
entries.label: Story
meta: Aired: August 18 to October 13, 2022 · 9 episodes · Phase 4 · Set in: 2024 to 2025 · Watch after: Thor: Love and Thunder
entries.story: Lawyer Jennifer Walters gets Hulk powers after a car crash mixes her blood with her cousin Bruce Banner's, but unlike Bruce, she stays fully in control as She-Hulk. She takes a job running a new superhuman law division, where her clients include the reformed Emil Blonsky (the Abomination from The Incredible Hulk) and the sorcerer Wong, and she has to deal with dating, online trolls and an online hate group called Intelligencia, led by a man named Todd, who steals her blood. She also works and flirts with Matt Murdock, Daredevil. In the comedic finale, Jennifer literally breaks through her Disney+ menu screen into Marvel Studios to argue with the artificial intelligence that writes the stories, K.E.V.I.N., and rewrites her own ending. Bruce returns from space with his son Skaar.
credits: Episodes 1 to 4: Short comedy scenes (Bruce revealing a secret about Steve Rogers, Jen helping her parents, a dance with Megan Thee Stallion, Wong watching television).
Episode 9 (mid-credits): Wong breaks Blonsky out of prison again.

entries.title: Werewolf by Night
entries.label: Story
entries.story: In a black-and-white homage to 1930s monster films, monster hunters gather at the eerie estate of the late Ulysses Bloodstone to compete for his powerful gem, the Bloodstone, in a hunt for a captured creature. Among the hunters are his estranged daughter Elsa and a mysterious man named Jack Russell, who is secretly a werewolf and has come to rescue his friend Ted, the swamp creature Man-Thing. Elsa and Jack team up, Jack transforms and kills most of the hunters, and Elsa ends up with the Bloodstone. It introduces the supernatural corner of the Marvel universe.
credits: None.

entries.title: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special
entries.label: Story
meta: Released: November 25, 2022 · a 44-minute special · Phase 4 · Set in: between Thor: Love and Thunder and Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3
entries.story: Mantis and Drax fly to Earth on a mission to find the perfect Christmas present for a gloomy Peter Quill, who misses Gamora: the actor Kevin Bacon, whom they kidnap from Hollywood. After some chaos, Kevin Bacon agrees to put on a Christmas party for the Guardians. Mantis then gives Quill a real present: the revelation that she is his half-sister, since both are children of Ego. The special also shows that the Guardians have bought Knowhere from the Collector and that Cosmo the space dog has joined the team.
credits: Post-credits: Rocket and Cosmo decorate Groot as a Christmas tree; the decorations fall off, and Rocket jokes they will need another special.

entries.title: Secret Invasion
entries.label: Story
meta: Aired: June 21 to July 26, 2023 · 6 episodes · Phase 5 · Set in: 2026 · Watch after: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 (and before The Marvels)
entries.story: Nick Fury returns to Earth from his space station after years away, because the Skrull refugees he promised to help (in Captain Marvel) have grown tired of waiting for a home. A radical Skrull named Gravik is leading an army of shape-shifting Skrulls who have replaced people in positions of power all over the world, and plans to provoke a world war between the United States and Russia so humans destroy themselves. Gravik kills Maria Hill and later Talos, and it is revealed that James Rhodes (War Machine) has been a Skrull impostor named Raava for some time, and that Fury's own wife Varra is a Skrull. Gravik and Talos's daughter G'iah both gain a mix of powers from the DNA of heroes and villains (the "Harvest"), and G'iah kills Gravik. The President of the United States declares war on all aliens on Earth, and Fury leaves for space.
credits: None.

entries.title: Loki, Season 2
entries.label: Story
meta: Aired: October 5 to November 9, 2023 · 6 episodes · Phase 5 · Set in: outside of time · Watch after: Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania (whose post-credits scene leads in)
entries.story: Loki is uncontrollably "time-slipping" between past and future, and the Time Variance Authority is in chaos after He Who Remains' death. Loki, Mobius, Sylvie and the agency's engineer Ouroboros ("O.B.") race to save the Temporal Loom, the machine that holds the branching timelines together, which is overloading as the multiverse grows. They track down Victor Timely, a 19th-century inventor and variant of He Who Remains, and Timely dies when the Loom explodes. Loki learns to control time-slipping and relives the disaster again and again trying to fix it, before realizing the only answer is sacrifice. He destroys the Loom, takes the throne at the End of Time, and holds the timelines together with his own hands as a living "World Tree," becoming the God of Stories.
credits: Episode 1 (mid-credits): Sylvie walks into a McDonald's in 1982.

entries.title: Echo
entries.label: Story
meta: Released: January 9, 2024 (all episodes at once) · 5 episodes · Phase 5 · Set in: 2025 · Watch after: Hawkeye
entries.story: Maya Lopez, the deaf Native American commander from Hawkeye, survived shooting Wilson Fisk and returns to her Choctaw hometown in Oklahoma to escape him. An early flashback shows her fighting Daredevil. Through visions of her ancestors, she discovers she has inherited a healing power passed down through the women of her family. Fisk comes for her, and with the help of her family, Maya uses her power to make him relive the pain of his childhood. Shaken, Fisk leaves.
credits: Episode 5 (mid-credits): Fisk watches news coverage of the New York mayoral race, planning his next move. (This leads into Daredevil: Born Again.)

entries.title: Agatha All Along
entries.label: Story
meta: Aired: September 18 to October 30, 2024 · 9 episodes · Phase 5 · Set in: a few years after WandaVision · Watch after: Deadpool & Wolverine
entries.story: Agatha Harkness is still trapped in Westview as "Agnes," until a teenager known only as "Teen" breaks the spell. He wants to walk the Witches' Road, a legendary magical path that grants a witch's deepest desire, and Agatha agrees to gather a coven of struggling witches to walk it with them. Along the road, each witch faces a deadly trial, and several die. "Teen" turns out to be Billy Maximoff, the son Wanda created, whose soul ended up in the body of a teenager named William Kaplan; and the mysterious Rio Vidal turns out to be Death itself, and Agatha's former lover. Agatha sacrifices herself to save Billy and returns as a ghost, becoming his guide as they set off to find Billy's brother Tommy.
credits: None.

entries.title: Daredevil: Born Again, Season 1
entries.label: Story
meta: Aired: March 4 to April 15, 2025 · 9 episodes · Phase 5 · Set in: late 2025 to early 2027 · Watch after: Captain America: Brave New World (its story follows Echo; ideally watch the Netflix Daredevil seasons first)
entries.story: The hitman Bullseye kills Matt Murdock's best friend and law partner Foggy Nelson, and Matt nearly kills Bullseye in revenge. A year later, Matt has given up being Daredevil, and his old enemy Wilson Fisk has been elected mayor of New York, promising to crack down on masked vigilantes. Matt defends a former hero, Hector Ayala (White Tiger), who is later murdered by a member of Fisk's new anti-vigilante police task force. Matt also tracks a serial killer called Muse, and learns that Fisk's wife Vanessa was the one who hired Bullseye to kill Foggy. In the finale, Fisk declares martial law, imprisons vigilantes (including Frank Castle, the Punisher) in a secret prison at the Red Hook docks, and Matt begins gathering a resistance.
credits: Episode 9 (mid-credits): The Punisher breaks a guard's arm and escapes from Fisk's prison.

entries.title: Ironheart
entries.label: Story
meta: Aired: June 24 to July 1, 2025 · 6 episodes · Phase 5 · Set in: about six months after Black Panther: Wakanda Forever · Watch after: Thunderbolts*
entries.story: Riri Williams, the teenage genius from Wakanda Forever, is expelled from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and returns home to Chicago to keep building her advanced armor. Desperate for money, she joins a crew of thieves led by Parker Robbins, known as the Hood, whose powerful magic cloak she does not understand. She also builds an artificial intelligence modelled on her late best friend, Natalie. Parker grows more violent and corrupted by the cloak, and Riri fights and defeats him. The cloak's true source is revealed to be Mephisto, a demon-like ruler of a hellish realm, who offers Riri a deal to bring Natalie back; Riri accepts, and a mark spreads up her arm.
credits: Episode 6 (mid-credits): Parker visits a magic shop asking for "big magic."

entries.title: Eyes of Wakanda
entries.label: Story
meta: Released: August 1, 2025 (all episodes at once) · 4 episodes · Phase 6 · Set in: across Wakanda's history, ending just before Black Panther · Watch after: The Fantastic Four: First Steps
entries.story: An animated anthology about the Hatut Zeraze ("War Dogs"), Wakanda's secret spies, who travel the world through history recovering stolen vibranium. Episodes take place in ancient Crete in 1260 BC (a warrior named Noni), at the Trojan War (B'Kai, who appears as the hero Memnon), in 1400 AD (where a War Dog meets an Iron Fist, the martial-arts hero from the city of K'un-Lun), and in 1896 Ethiopia, where a future Black Panther from 500 years ahead warns of an alien "Horde." Marvel has confirmed it is part of the main timeline, unlike What If...?. The final scene shows Erik Killmonger just before the museum heist in Black Panther.
credits: None known.

entries.title: Wonder Man
entries.label: Story
meta: Released: January 27, 2026 (all episodes at once) · 8 episodes · Phase 6 · Watch after: The Fantastic Four: First Steps
entries.story: Simon Williams is a struggling actor in Los Angeles who secretly has powerful ionic energy abilities, which he hides because a Hollywood rule, the "Doorman Clause," bans people with powers from film sets. He befriends Trevor Slattery, the washed-up actor who played the fake "Mandarin" in Iron Man 3, without knowing Trevor is spying on him for the Department of Damage Control. Together they audition for a remake of an old superhero film called "Wonder Man." Simon's powers explode on set, and Trevor takes the blame and goes to prison. Simon wins the role, breaks Trevor out, and flies away with him, while a Damage Control agent decides Simon might be useful someday. (A second season was announced and then cancelled in July 2026.)
credits: None.

entries.title: Daredevil: Born Again, Season 2
entries.label: Story
meta: Aired: March 24 to May 5, 2026 · 8 episodes · Phase 6 · Watch after: Wonder Man (and Daredevil: Born Again season 1)
entries.story: Six months later, Mayor Fisk rules New York under martial law and keeps his secret prison running at Red Hook. Matt fights back as Daredevil while Bullseye unmasks him and begins killing members of the task force, and Jessica Jones (Krysten Ritter, from the Netflix show) teams up with Matt to destroy Fisk's weapons. Vanessa Fisk is fatally wounded and dies, and Matt chooses to spare Fisk after a brutal fight. To clear his friend Karen Page in court, Matt calls Fisk as a witness and publicly reveals he is Daredevil. Fisk kills protesters, then takes a deal and goes into exile, the task force is disbanded, and Matt is arrested and jailed. (A third and reportedly final season is planned for March 2027.)
credits: None.

entries.title: The Punisher: One Last Kill
entries.label: Story
meta: Released: May 12, 2026 · a special of about 50 minutes · Phase 6 · Watch after: Daredevil: Born Again season 2 (and before Spider-Man: Brand New Day)
entries.story: Frank Castle, the Punisher, has finished his war of revenge for his murdered family and feels he has nothing left to live for, haunted by visions of the people he lost. A vision of his daughter Lisa stops him from ending his life at his family's grave. Crime boss Ma Gnucci puts a bounty on him and floods his apartment building with killers. While protecting a local shopkeeper's family, Frank finds a reason to keep going, and puts on a new version of his skull costume. It bridges the gap between the Netflix Punisher show and his role in Spider-Man: Brand New Day.
credits: None.

entries.title: VisionQuest
entries.label: Story
meta: Aired: October 13 to November 10, 2026 · 8 episodes · Phase 6 · Set in: years after WandaVision, around the time of Spider-Man: Brand New Day · Watch after: Spider-Man: Brand New Day (and before Avengers: Doomsday)
entries.story: The White Vision who flew away at the end of WandaVision has his memories back but no emotions, and is searching for who he is now. His mind turns out to be shared with other artificial intelligences in human form, including his old enemy Ultron (James Spader, returning from Age of Ultron), the android Jocasta, and versions of Tony Stark's assistant programs such as J.A.R.V.I.S., F.R.I.D.A.Y. and E.D.I.T.H. A bounty hunter named Paladin hunts Vision, while Jocasta, operating as a killer called "Butcherbird," chases a secret nanotechnology project. Vision journeys into his own programming and confronts his grief over Wanda and their sons, and Tommy Maximoff's soul is revealed to be living in a teenager named Thomas Shepherd, whom Vision claims as his son. The mysterious "Client" who wears Ultron's face turns out to be Virgil Horton, the scientist who rebuilt Vision's body for S.W.O.R.D. and who built Jocasta's body, then erased her memory of him. He plans to move his own mind into Vision and use the nanobots to force the world into obedience. In the finale, Jocasta turns on Virgil, is shot, and frees the real Ultron before she dies in his arms. Ultron crushes Virgil, then sends the nanobots toward London. Vision traps Ultron inside a sitcom-style simulation, an echo of WandaVision, and talks him into calling the attack off. Tommy reaches his twin Billy through magic, Billy (still coached by Agatha's ghost) opens a portal to join him, and together the brothers restart their father, who returns in his red-and-green form. Vision and his sons plan a life together as a family, and when Tommy asks about their mother, Vision says they might yet see her again. Ultron survives, and phones Vision to say he has not decided what to do with his freedom.
credits: Episodes 1 to 7: None.
Episode 8 (first credits scene): Ultron stands alone in the Horton house holding the chip that stores Jocasta's program, a hint that he could bring her back.

Episode 8 (second credits scene): Wanda's apparent death under Mount Wundagore in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness replays, then continues: Doctor Doom (Robert Downey Jr.) lifts the rubble and commands, "Scarlet Witch, awaken." Wanda's eyes open. (This sets up her return in Avengers: Doomsday.)
notes: Note: The finale, "Forever," came out on November 10, 2026. A second season has not been announced. Copies sent to reviewers left out the second credits scene, so some early write-ups mention only the Ultron scene.

entries.title: Daredevil
entries.label: Story
entries.story: Matt Murdock, blinded as a boy by a chemical spill that heightened his other senses to superhuman levels, is a lawyer by day in Hell's Kitchen, New York, with his best friend Foggy Nelson and their assistant Karen Page, and a masked vigilante by night. Season 1 pits him against crime lord Wilson Fisk, who dreams of rebuilding the neighborhood and destroys anyone in his way, and ends with Fisk in prison and Matt in his red Daredevil suit. Season 2 introduces Frank Castle, the Punisher, a brutal former Marine killing the gangs who murdered his family, and Elektra, Matt's deadly ex-girlfriend, in a war with the ancient ninja cult the Hand. Season 3 follows Fisk manipulating his way out of prison and turning a disturbed FBI marksman, Benjamin "Dex" Poindexter, into the killer later known as Bullseye; Matt sends Fisk back to prison and reunites with Foggy and Karen.
credits: None.

entries.title: Jessica Jones
entries.label: Story
entries.story: Jessica Jones, a hard-drinking private investigator with super strength, is haunted by Kilgrave, a man with the power to control minds who once forced her to do terrible things. Season 1 follows her hunt for Kilgrave, which ends when she kills him. Later seasons explore the experiments that gave her powers, her troubled mother, and a serial killer, while her adoptive sister Trish Walker becomes a dangerous vigilante called Hellcat. Jessica returns in Daredevil: Born Again season 2.
credits: None.

entries.title: Luke Cage
entries.label: Story
entries.story: Luke Cage, a former prisoner who gained unbreakable skin and super strength from an illegal experiment, becomes the bulletproof protector of Harlem. He battles nightclub owner Cottonmouth, crooked politician Mariah Dillard, and the villain Diamondback, who turns out to be his half-brother. In season 2 he clashes with the Jamaican gangster Bushmaster, and by the end Luke takes over Mariah's club, Harlem's Paradise, to control the neighborhood's crime from inside.
credits: None.

entries.title: Iron Fist
entries.label: Story
entries.story: Danny Rand, the heir to a billion-dollar company who was presumed dead after a plane crash, returns to New York after 15 years training in the mystical city of K'un-Lun, where he earned the power of the Iron Fist, a glowing fist of chi energy. He fights to reclaim his company and discovers it has been infiltrated by the Hand. In season 2 his friend-turned-rival Davos steals the Iron Fist power, and Danny's partner Colleen Wing takes it on herself, while Danny leaves to explore the origins of the Iron Fist.
credits: None.

entries.title: The Defenders
entries.label: Story
entries.story: Daredevil, Jessica Jones, Luke Cage and Iron Fist are drawn together when the Hand, led by the ancient Alexandra and her resurrected weapon, Elektra (brought back from the dead by the Hand), plan to dig up a mystical substance beneath New York that would destroy the city. The four mismatched heroes reluctantly team up. They defeat the Hand under a skyscraper that collapses on top of Matt and Elektra. Matt is presumed dead but survives, setting up Daredevil season 3.
credits: None.

entries.title: The Punisher
entries.label: Story
entries.story: Frank Castle, believing he has killed everyone responsible for his family's murder, discovers a conspiracy reaching into the military and a covert operation he took part in, and teams up with a former National Security Agency analyst, Micro, to expose it. He discovers his best friend Billy Russo betrayed him, and leaves Billy's face scarred (becoming the villain Jigsaw). In season 2 Frank protects a teenage girl from a religious assassin and finally kills Russo, embracing his life as the Punisher.
credits: None.

entries.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.
entries.label: Story
entries.story: Agent Phil Coulson, mysteriously alive after dying in The Avengers, leads a small team of S.H.I.E.L.D. agents investigating strange and superhuman cases. Its first season ties directly into Captain America: The Winter Soldier, when the team discovers HYDRA has infiltrated S.H.I.E.L.D. from within, and later episodes react to Age of Ultron. As the show goes on it follows its own path, with the Inhumans (people with alien-given powers), Ghost Rider, and time travel to the future and the past, contradicting the films more and more. It ends with the team saving the world one last time and going their separate ways.

entries.title: Agent Carter
entries.label: Story
entries.story: In 1946, Peggy Carter, grieving Steve Rogers, works at the Strategic Scientific Reserve, where her male colleagues treat her as a secretary. Secretly helped by Howard Stark's butler Edwin Jarvis, she clears Howard's name when his inventions are stolen and used as weapons, and uncovers the Soviet program that later produces Black Widow. In season 2 she moves to Los Angeles to battle a scientist who absorbs a mysterious dark energy. It fits well with the films, but is not on the official timeline.

entries.title: Inhumans
entries.label: Story
entries.story: The royal family of the Inhumans, a race with powers living in the hidden city of Attilan on the Moon, is overthrown by the king's brother Maximus and stranded in Hawaii. Led by Black Bolt, whose voice can level buildings, they try to retake their home. Poorly received and cancelled after one season.

entries.title: Runaways
entries.label: Story
entries.story: A group of Los Angeles teenagers discover their wealthy parents secretly run a criminal cult called the Pride, which performs human sacrifices. The teens run away together, discover their own powers and abilities, and fight both their parents and the alien beings behind them. Season 3 crosses over with Cloak & Dagger.

entries.title: Cloak & Dagger
entries.label: Story
entries.story: Two New Orleans teenagers from very different backgrounds, Tandy Bowen and Tyrone Johnson, gain linked powers of light and darkness after a disaster at an oil rig owned by the corporation Roxxon. Tandy can sense people's hopes, Tyrone their fears. They fight corrupt police and corporate villains together while slowly becoming partners.

entries.title: Helstrom
entries.label: Story
entries.story: Daimon and Ana Helstrom, the adult children of a mysterious serial killer, hunt demons and people possessed by them in Portland. It was stripped of the Marvel branding before release and is not considered part of the main story.

entries.title: X-Men
entries.label: Story
meta: Released: July 14, 2000 · Set in: "the not too distant future" (with a 1944 opening at the Auschwitz concentration camp) · Timeline: original
entries.story: A young Erik Lehnsherr's power over metal first appears when he is separated from his parents at Auschwitz. Decades later, teenage runaway Rogue, whose touch drains the life and powers of anyone she touches, meets Logan, known as Wolverine, a gruff loner with healing powers, metal claws and no memory of his past. They are rescued from Magneto's henchman Sabretooth by Storm and Cyclops and taken to Professor Xavier's school, where Logan meets Jean Grey. Magneto and his Brotherhood of Mutants (Mystique, Toad, Sabretooth) plan to use a machine to turn the world's leaders, gathered on Ellis Island, into mutants, powered by Rogue's ability to absorb his power, though the change is unstable and kills the anti-mutant Senator Kelly. The X-Men stop the machine atop the Statue of Liberty, and Logan saves the dying Rogue by letting her absorb his healing. Magneto is imprisoned in a plastic cell, where Xavier visits him to play chess, and Logan leaves to search for his past at Alkali Lake.
credits: None.

entries.title: X2
entries.label: Story
entries.story: A mind-controlled teleporting mutant, Nightcrawler, attacks the President in the White House, giving military scientist Colonel William Stryker an excuse to raid Xavier's school and capture the Professor. Stryker, who turns out to be the man who gave Wolverine his metal skeleton, plans to use his own mutant son and a copy of Xavier's mutant-tracking machine, Cerebro, to kill every mutant on Earth. The X-Men are forced to team up with Magneto and Mystique, but Magneto secretly reverses the machine to target every human instead. Storm and Nightcrawler free Xavier just in time, and Logan kills Stryker's assassin Lady Deathstrike and leaves Stryker to drown. As the dam at Alkali Lake bursts, Jean Grey sacrifices herself to hold back the flood so the X-Men's jet can escape. The last shot shows a fiery bird shape under the lake: the Phoenix.
credits: None.

entries.title: X-Men: The Last Stand
entries.label: Story
meta: Released: May 26, 2006 · Timeline: original (later erased by Days of Future Past)
entries.story: A pharmaceutical company announces a "cure" that can permanently remove mutant powers, made from a boy named Leech, splitting mutants over whether they should want it. Jean Grey returns from the lake, but she has become the Phoenix, an unstoppable split personality with almost limitless power; she kills her love Cyclops and then disintegrates Professor Xavier, and joins Magneto. Magneto leads an army of mutants against the cure facility on Alcatraz Island, and the X-Men, led by Storm and Wolverine, fight to stop him; Magneto is stripped of his powers by a cure dart. Logan is forced to kill Jean, who begs him to save her from herself. Rogue chooses to take the cure.
credits: Final scene (before the credits): Magneto sits alone at a chessboard in a park and makes a metal chess piece twitch, hinting his powers are returning.
Post-credits: Dr. Moira MacTaggert checks on a patient in a coma, who speaks in Xavier's voice, revealing Xavier transferred his mind into this man's body before he died.

entries.title: X-Men Origins: Wolverine
entries.label: Story
entries.story: In 1845 Canada, young James Howlett discovers his bone claws and flees with his half-brother Victor, and the two fight side by side through the American Civil War, both World Wars and Vietnam, before joining a secret mutant team led by William Stryker. Logan leaves the team in disgust and lives peacefully with his girlfriend Kayla Silverfox, until she appears to be murdered by Victor (Sabretooth). For revenge, Logan agrees to have the nearly indestructible metal adamantium bonded to his skeleton in Stryker's Weapon X program, then learns Stryker staged everything. At Stryker's base on Three Mile Island, Logan and Victor fight Weapon XI, a mutant made from the powers of many others (including Wade Wilson, called "Deadpool" here, with his mouth sewn shut). Kayla dies after freeing captive young mutants, and Stryker shoots Logan in the head with an adamantium bullet, wiping his memory.
credits: Mid-credits: Stryker is detained by military police for questioning about the murder of a general.
Post-credits: In Japan, Logan drinks in a bar and says he is "drinking to remember." (Some versions instead show Weapon XI's severed head opening its eyes.)

entries.title: X-Men: First Class
entries.label: Story
meta: Released: June 3, 2011 · Set in: 1962 (with a 1944 opening) · Timeline: before the split (belongs to both)
entries.story: A prequel showing how the X-Men began. Young Charles Xavier, a charming telepath, and Erik Lehnsherr, a Holocaust survivor hunting the Nazi scientist who murdered his mother, become friends while helping Central Intelligence Agency agent Moira MacTaggert. That scientist is Sebastian Shaw, now leader of the Hellfire Club, who plans to start a nuclear war between the United States and the Soviet Union so that mutants can rule. Charles and Erik recruit and train young mutants, including Charles's adopted sister Raven (Mystique), Hank McCoy (Beast), Havok and Banshee. During the Cuban Missile Crisis, Erik kills Shaw and then turns the missiles on the human fleets; a bullet deflected by Erik hits Charles in the spine, leaving him unable to walk. Erik, now calling himself Magneto, leaves with Raven to form the Brotherhood, and Charles starts his school.
credits: None.

entries.title: The Wolverine
entries.label: Story
entries.story: Haunted by killing Jean Grey, Logan is living as a hermit when a young woman named Yukio brings him to Tokyo to say goodbye to Yashida, a soldier he saved during the atomic bombing of Nagasaki in 1945, now a dying billionaire. Yashida offers to take away Logan's healing powers so he can finally die. Logan protects Yashida's granddaughter Mariko from yakuza gangsters, while a mutant named Viper secretly weakens his healing. Yashida faked his death, and inside a giant adamantium robot, the Silver Samurai, tries to steal Logan's healing power, cutting off Logan's adamantium claws. Logan's original bone claws grow back, Mariko kills Yashida, and Logan leaves Japan with Yukio.
credits: Mid-credits: Two years later at an airport, Logan is approached by Magneto, whose powers have returned, and a living Professor Xavier, who warn him of a dangerous new threat to all mutants. (This leads into Days of Future Past.)

entries.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
entries.label: Story
meta: Released: May 23, 2014 · Set in: 2023 and 1973 · Timeline: the film that creates the revised timeline
entries.story: In a dark 2023, giant mutant-hunting robots called Sentinels have killed most mutants and the humans who helped them. The surviving X-Men, including an old Xavier and Magneto, have Kitty Pryde send Logan's mind back into his 1973 body to stop the event that started it: Mystique's assassination of Bolivar Trask, the Sentinels' inventor, after which her captured DNA made the Sentinels unbeatable. In 1973, Logan recruits a broken, drug-dependent young Charles and Hank, and they break young Erik out of a prison under the Pentagon with help from the super-fast Quicksilver. Erik turns on them and attacks the Sentinels' public unveiling in Washington by dropping a stadium around the White House, but Mystique chooses to spare Trask, changing the future. Logan wakes up in a new, peaceful 2023 where Jean, Cyclops and the school are alive. In 1973, the "Stryker" who pulls Logan's body out of the river is revealed to be Mystique in disguise.
credits: Post-credits: In ancient Egypt, a powerful mutant, En Sabah Nur (Apocalypse), builds the pyramids with his mind while four horsemen watch.
notes: The Rogue Cut (2015 home release, about 17 minutes longer) adds a mission in which Xavier, Magneto and Iceman rescue Rogue in the future, and Rogue takes over from Kitty in holding Logan's mind in the past. It also adds a mid-credits scene of Trask locked in Magneto's old Pentagon cell.

entries.title: Deadpool
entries.label: Story
meta: Released: February 12, 2016 · Set in: the present day · Timeline: revised (this Deadpool is unrelated to the one in Origins: Wolverine)
entries.story: Wade Wilson, a fast-talking former special forces soldier working as a mercenary, falls in love with Vanessa, then learns he has terminal cancer. A shadowy program promises a cure, and its sadistic leader Ajax (real name Francis) tortures Wade until his mutant healing kicks in, curing the cancer but leaving his skin horribly scarred, and leaves him for dead. Unkillable and constantly joking to the audience, Wade becomes the masked Deadpool and hunts Ajax for a cure to his scars. Ajax kidnaps Vanessa, and the X-Men's Colossus and his trainee Negasonic Teenage Warhead reluctantly help Wade storm a scrapyard where a wrecked Helicarrier stands. Wade kills Ajax and reunites with Vanessa.
credits: Post-credits: Deadpool in a bathrobe spoofs the end of the film Ferris Bueller's Day Off and announces that the time-traveling soldier Cable will appear in the sequel.

entries.title: X-Men: Apocalypse
entries.label: Story
entries.story: Apocalypse, the world's first and most powerful mutant, wakes up in Cairo after thousands of years and decides to wipe out modern civilization. He recruits four mutants as his "Horsemen": a young Storm, Psylocke, Angel (who he turns into Archangel) and a grieving Magneto, whose wife and daughter were just killed by police in Poland. He kidnaps Xavier to take over his body and his telepathy. Stryker captures several X-Men and takes them to Alkali Lake, where they free Wolverine (in his feral Weapon X state) before escaping. In the final battle in Cairo, a young Jean Grey unleashes her full Phoenix power and destroys Apocalypse. Xavier is left bald, Magneto helps rebuild the school, and Mystique and Beast begin training a new X-Men team including Cyclops, Jean, Storm, Nightcrawler and Quicksilver.
credits: Post-credits: Men in black suits collect a vial of Wolverine's blood from the Weapon X facility, labeled for the Essex Corporation (a hint at the villain Mister Sinister).

entries.title: Logan
entries.label: Story
meta: Released: March 3, 2017 · Set in: 2029 · Timeline: deliberately unclear (Deadpool & Wolverine later treats it as part of Deadpool's universe)
entries.story: In 2029, no new mutant has been born in 25 years and most of the X-Men are dead. An aging, sick Logan, whose healing is failing, works as a limousine driver near the Mexican border and secretly cares for a 90-year-old Charles Xavier, whose brain disease causes deadly psychic seizures. A nurse begs Logan to take a mute girl, Laura, to a place called "Eden" in North Dakota; Laura is X-23, a girl created in a lab from Logan's DNA, with claws of her own. Hunted by mercenaries called the Reavers and a deadly clone of Logan (X-24), the three go on a road trip, and X-24 kills Xavier. Logan delivers Laura and the other escaped mutant children to the border, and dies after the final battle in which Laura kills X-24 with an adamantium bullet. The children bury him and Laura turns his grave's cross on its side into an "X."
credits: None.

entries.title: Deadpool 2
entries.label: Story
entries.story: When Vanessa is killed by a gang, Wade tries to end his life and is taken to Xavier's school by Colossus. While on a trainee X-Men mission, Wade meets Russell, an angry teenage mutant who can throw fireballs (Firefist), who is abused at a mutant orphanage. Cable, a cyborg soldier from the future, arrives to kill Russell, because in his future Russell becomes a murderer who kills Cable's family. Wade forms his own team, X-Force, which almost all die on their first mission (the lucky mutant Domino survives). Russell teams up with the giant mutant Juggernaut, and Wade takes a bullet meant for Russell, changing his future; Cable uses his last time travel charge to save Wade's life.
credits: Mid-credits: Using Cable's repaired time travel device, Wade saves Vanessa and a team member, kills the "Deadpool" from X-Men Origins: Wolverine (while Wolverine watches in confusion), and shoots actor Ryan Reynolds as he reads the script for his much-mocked film Green Lantern.
notes: Once Upon a Deadpool (December 2018) is a family-friendly re-edit framed as Deadpool reading the story to actor Fred Savage, ending with a tribute to Stan Lee.

entries.title: Dark Phoenix
entries.label: Story
meta: Released: June 7, 2019 · Set in: 1992 · Timeline: revised (the last main Fox X-Men film)
entries.story: On a rescue mission to a damaged space shuttle, Jean Grey absorbs a mysterious cosmic force that makes her vastly more powerful but unstable. She learns Xavier hid the truth that her father is still alive, loses control, and accidentally kills Mystique. Shape-shifting aliens, the D'Bari, led by Vuk, want the force for themselves. Beast and Magneto both want revenge on Jean, while Xavier and Cyclops try to save her. In a final battle on a train, Jean takes control of the power, destroys the D'Bari, and flies into space, apparently dying. The school is renamed the "Jean Grey School," and Xavier retires to Paris, where Erik joins him for chess while a phoenix shape appears in the sky.
credits: None.

entries.title: The New Mutants
entries.label: Story
meta: Released: August 28, 2020 · Timeline: loosely connected (the film itself makes few links to the others)
entries.story: Dani Moonstar, a Cheyenne teenager, is the only survivor of a disaster that destroys her reservation. She wakes up in a remote hospital run by Dr. Cecilia Reyes alongside four other young mutants, each haunted by their past. The teens are attacked by their own worst fears, and discover that the hospital is run by the Essex Corporation, which is training them as weapons and plans to kill Dani. Dani's fears take the form of the Demon Bear, a giant monster that was the real cause of her reservation's destruction, and it kills Dr. Reyes. With the help of her friends, Dani calms the bear, and at dawn the group leaves the hospital together.
credits: None.

entries.title: Deadpool & Wolverine
entries.tag: The farewell to the Fox universe
entries.label: The mutant story
meta: Released: July 26, 2024 · Set in: Earth-10005 and the Void · see entry #34 in Part 1
entries.story: Six years after Deadpool 2, Wade learns from the Time Variance Authority that his whole universe, the world of the Fox X-Men films, is dying because its most important person, Logan, died in Logan. Wade recruits a different Wolverine from another universe (the "worst" one, who let his X-Men die) and is exiled with him to the Void, a wasteland where erased characters from the Fox films (Blade, Elektra, X-23 and Gambit, and the Human Torch) are trapped and ruled by Cassandra Nova, Charles Xavier's evil twin sister. The two heroes save their universe together, and this Wolverine stays to take Logan's place. It closes the Fox era and opens the door for Fox characters to enter the main multiverse. Credit scenes: a behind-the-scenes tribute to 20 years of Fox Marvel films (during the credits) and Johnny Storm's crude rant about Cassandra Nova (post-credits).

entries.title: X-Men '97
entries.label: Story
meta: Aired: Season 1 March 20 to May 15, 2024 (10 episodes); Season 2 July 1 to August 12, 2026 (9 episodes)
entries.story: A direct continuation of the beloved 1990s cartoon X-Men: The Animated Series, picking up after Professor X has left Earth and leaving Cyclops to lead the team under the rule that Magneto, now reformed, is in charge of the school. Season 1 follows the destruction of the mutant nation of Genosha by Sentinels, Magneto's revenge on humanity, and a devastating battle with the villain Bastion, ending with the X-Men scattered across time. Season 2 follows them stranded in the ancient past, the present and the far future, facing Apocalypse. It is set in the cartoon's own universe, separate from both the films and the main story, but it is highly recommended for anyone who wants to understand the X-Men's biggest comic storylines.
credits: Not tracked in this guide; the show stands on its own and does not set up the films.

entries.title: The Fantastic Four
entries.label: Story
meta: Made: 1992 to 1994 · Status: never released; known only from bootleg copies
entries.story: A German producer, Bernd Eichinger, held the film rights and had to start making a film before they expired at the end of 1992, so he made a very cheap version (about $1 million) with low-budget producer Roger Corman. College friends Reed Richards and Victor von Doom run an experiment with a passing comet that goes wrong, and Victor is believed dead. Ten years later, Reed, Sue, Johnny and Ben fly into space to study the comet, but a jewel thief called the Jeweler has swapped the diamond protecting them for a fake, so they are exposed to cosmic radiation and gain powers. Doom, alive and in armor, captures them, and the Jeweler kidnaps Ben's love interest, the blind sculptor Alicia Masters. The team escapes, Johnny redirects Doom's laser away from New York, and Reed and Sue marry. The planned premiere was cancelled, and Marvel's Avi Arad later said he bought the film so it would never be shown; the full story is told in the documentary Doomed! (2015).
credits: None.

entries.title: Fantastic Four
entries.label: Story
entries.story: Struggling scientist Reed Richards and his friend, astronaut Ben Grimm, ask Reed's former college rival, billionaire Victor von Doom, to fund a trip to Doom's space station to study a cosmic storm, joined by Reed's ex-girlfriend Sue Storm (now Doom's employee) and her brother Johnny, the pilot. The storm arrives early and gives all four powers, and Doom, too, slowly turns into living metal with electrical powers. The team becomes famous after a rescue on the Brooklyn Bridge, but Ben, turned into a rock-covered monster, loses his fiancée and suffers. Doom manipulates Ben into using Reed's machine to turn human, then captures Reed and attacks the team's headquarters, the Baxter Building. Ben turns back into the Thing to help, and the four defeat Doom together by heating him with Johnny's flames and then freezing him with water. Doom's frozen body is shipped home to Latveria, Reed proposes to Sue, and Ben starts dating Alicia Masters. (Johnny Storm is played by Chris Evans, who went on to play Captain America and played Johnny again in Deadpool & Wolverine.)
credits: None.

entries.title: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
entries.label: Story
entries.story: As Reed and Sue prepare for their wedding, a mysterious silver figure on a flying surfboard races around the world, leaving giant craters and draining London's River Thames. Johnny chases the Silver Surfer, and a touch from him makes Johnny swap powers with anyone he touches. The Surfer's energy also frees and heals Doctor Doom, who teams up with the United States military, captures the Surfer and steals his board, which turns out to be a beacon for Galactus, shown here as a giant cosmic cloud that devours planets. The Fantastic Four defeat Doom with Johnny absorbing all four powers at once, and return the board to the Surfer, who turns against his master and sacrifices himself to destroy Galactus. Reed and Sue finally marry in Japan.
credits: Mid-credits: The Silver Surfer's seemingly lifeless body floats in space, his eyes open, and his board flies back to him.

entries.title: Fantastic Four
entries.label: Story
entries.story: A darker reboot. Reed Richards and his best friend Ben Grimm have been building a teleporter since childhood. Reed is recruited by Dr. Franklin Storm and his children, Sue and Johnny, to build a "Quantum Gate" to another dimension with a bitter young genius, Victor von Doom. After a drunken late-night decision, Reed, Johnny, Victor and Ben secretly travel to the alien world, which they call Planet Zero; Victor is lost there, and the trip changes the others' bodies (Sue is affected on the way back). A year later, the government uses them as weapons, and Victor returns fused to his suit with powerful mental abilities, kills many people (including Franklin Storm), and tries to destroy Earth using Planet Zero's energy. The four work together to defeat him and set up a new headquarters, naming themselves the Fantastic Four. (The director, Josh Trank, publicly disowned the version the studio released.)
credits: None.

entries.title: The Fantastic Four: First Steps
entries.label: The family's story
meta: Released: July 25, 2025 · Universe: Earth-828 · see entry #37 in Part 1
entries.story: In a bright, retro-futuristic version of 1964 on their own Earth (Earth-828), the Fantastic Four (Pedro Pascal as Reed, Vanessa Kirby as Sue, Joseph Quinn as Johnny, Ebon Moss-Bachrach as Ben) have been beloved heroes for four years, with their own robot helper H.E.R.B.I.E. and their own cartoon show. Sue's pregnancy turns the film into a story about parenthood: when Galactus offers to spare Earth only in exchange for their newborn son Franklin, Reed and Sue refuse, and the world turns on them. Johnny reaches the Silver Surfer, Shalla-Bal, by learning her history, and Ben helps the Mole Man shelter New York's people underground. Sue nearly dies holding back Galactus while the Surfer pushes him through a portal, and baby Franklin brings his mother back to life, revealing that he has incredible cosmic powers. Credit scenes: four years later, Sue finds young Franklin with Doctor Doom (mid-credits); H.E.R.B.I.E. switches off the old Fantastic Four cartoon (post-credits).
